Consider the following Sales Management schema:

| Relation | Attributes |
|---|---|
| Suppliers | $(sID,\ sName,\ address)$ |
| Parts | $(pID,\ pName,\ colour)$ |
| Catalog | $(sID,\ pID,\ price)$ |

Write the following SQL queries:

i) Find the name and ID of the suppliers whose address contains 'Manipal'. Sort the records in alphabetical order of their name, if two suppliers have same name then sort them in descending order of ID.
ii) Compute the suppliers name and ID who have sold the part with ID 10 at a price more than that supplied by supplier with ID 2.
iii) Find the supplier IDs who sold the part with ID 123 at a price more than its average selling price.
iv) Calculate the IDs of parts whose price is in the range of 500 and 1000. Eliminate duplicates from resulting relation.
v) Using appropriate SQL set operations, find all the suppliers who supplied blue coloured parts but their address did not contain 'Manipal'.
